entry.title: Combined summary - Boomerang: Bitcoin Cold Storage with Built-In Coercion Resistance
entry.summary: The Boomerang protocol has been developed as a sophisticated security mechanism catering primarily to significant bitcoin holders who are potentially vulnerable to both cyber and physical threats, such as forced transactions through coercion. This system intricately combines advanced technologies and strategic methodologies to enhance the security during withdrawals of bitcoins. It operates by making the withdrawal process unpredictable within a specified timeframe, which is termed the 'boomerang period'. During this phase, each participant's device, known as "Boomlet", randomly selects steps from a set range to complete transactions, thereby introducing an element of unpredictability that serves to deter potential attackers. Further enhancing its security measures, Boomerang incorporates a unique duress mechanism whereby users establish a pre-memorized "consent set" of five countries. In situations where a user faces coercion, they can subtly signal distress by deviating from this consent set during transaction verifications. This activates an alert to the Search and Rescue (SAR) teams without the attacker's knowledge, leveraging encrypted communications and the anonymity provided by various networks to initiate a rescue operation discreetly. The setup involves isolated devices and air-gapped communications to securely establish encryption keys and record the user's consent set, ensuring robust protection against different attack vectors including replay attacks and direct observation. Additionally, the email highlights recent improvements made to readme files, focusing on enhancing clarity and accessibility for users. This upgrade is essential for providing clearer guidance and facilitating better user experiences with software or systems, reflecting a commitment to high-quality documentation. Furthermore, the importance of incorporating a recovery plan alongside the main protective strategies in systems designed for long-term savings is emphasized. Introducing a straightforward recovery checklist and recommending practice sessions with smaller assets can significantly bolster the system's resilience and instill user confidence. The technical backbone of the Boomerang protocol, particularly the reliance on the Java card referred to as "Boomlet", is identified as a critical component. Current setups include a backup for the Boomlet, but lack a designated activation mechanism, suggesting an area for future enhancement to increase system robustness. Plans are underway to improve the reliability of other crucial elements such as the watchtower (WT) and SAR functionalities by adding multiple instances for redundancy, which will enhance fault tolerance. The inclusion of a recovery checklist into the ancillary list represents a proactive approach towards comprehensive disaster recovery preparedness and efficient management of potential system issues. For further insights into the dynamics of physical attacks on bitcoin and crypto-asset holders and how adaptive defense mechanisms can be, readers can explore detailed discussions at [this link](https://bitryonix.org/security/notes/001-2026-08-26-physical-attacks-on-bitcoin-and-crypto-asset-holders-an-adaptive-process-model).
